record.paper_title: Some open questions on morphological operators and representations in the deep learning era: A personal vision
record.context_brief: Unified algebraic theory for hybrid deep networks
record.original_question: What unified algebraic models can integrate standard deep-learning layers with morphological layers so that deep-learning architectures can be studied mathematically, including questions about order continuity, invariance, fixed points, decomposition, simplification, and the expressiveness of deep MMBB networks and hybrid deep networks?

evidence.quote: What kind of unified algebraic models, integrating standard layers and morphological layers can be used to mathematically study deep learning architectures? Is there any information on order continuity, on invariance and fixed points, on decomposition and simplification, etc., which can be inferred from these unified algebraic models? What is the expressiveness of deep MMBB networks and the hybrid deep networks?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A standard feed-forward neural network layer is a map of the form $x \mapsto \sigma(Wx+b)$, where $W$ is a linear operator, $b$ a bias, and $\sigma$ a pointwise nonlinearity; such layers are linear-plus-nonlinearity operators on a vector space. A morphological layer, by contrast, is built from the basic operators of mathematical morphology on a complete lattice $(L,\le)$: the dilation $\delta_b(x)(p) = \sup_{q} \{x(p-q)+b(q)\}$ and the erosion $\varepsilon_b(x)(p) = \inf_{q}\{x(p+q)-b(q)\}$, which are residuated/adjoint operators preserving suprema and infima respectively. Compositions of dilations and erosions (and their min/max/plus arithmetic, called the (max,+)/(min,+) semiring) yield the class of Matheron–Maragos basis-based (MMBB) operators, i.e.\ translation-invariant increasing operators representable as suprema of erosions (or infima of dilations) over a structuring-element basis. A "deep MMBB network" is a finite composition of such MMBB layers; a "hybrid deep network" is a finite composition that mixes standard linear+activation layers with morphological layers.

Problem. Develop a single algebraic framework — for instance, over an idempotent semiring, a complete lattice with a compatible module structure, or a tropical/(max,+)-linear algebra — in which both standard deep-learning layers and morphological layers appear as morphisms of one common category, such that the following questions can be formulated and answered within this framework for an arbitrary composition $F = L_n \circ \cdots \circ L_1$ of layers:

(a) Continuity: characterize when $F$ is order-continuous (preserves directed suprema and/or filtered infima) on its input lattice.

(b) Invariance: describe the group/monoid of transformations (translations, scalings, lattice automorphisms) under which $F$ is equivariant or invariant.

(c) Fixed points: give existence, structure, and computation of the set $\mathrm{Fix}(F)=\{x : F(x)=x\}$, including least and greatest fixed points when $F$ is increasing.

(d) Decomposition: prove a canonical decomposition theorem expressing $F$ in terms of elementary atoms (e.g.\ erosions, dilations, linear maps, activations) analogous to the Matheron representation of increasing translation-invariant operators.

(e) Simplification: identify algebraic rewriting rules that reduce $F$ to a minimal equivalent representative, and determine when such a normal form exists and is unique.

(f) Expressiveness: characterize, for deep MMBB networks and for hybrid deep networks, the class of input–output maps they can realize as a function of depth and width, and compare it to the classes realized by purely linear+ReLU networks and by purely morphological networks.

Provide the algebraic framework and resolve as many of (a)–(f) as possible within it.
artifact.status_search_result: A unified algebraic theory bringing standard and morphological deep-learning layers under one model—with proven results on order-continuity, invariance, fixed points, decomposition, simplification, and expressiveness for deep MMBB and hybrid networks—has not appeared. Partial progress exists via tropical-geometry analyses of ReLU networks (Zhang–Naitzat–Lim) and via lattice/morphological-network studies (Charisopoulos–Maragos, Velasco-Forero, Mondal et al.), but no comprehensive unified framework is established.

status_evidence.title: Tropical Geometry of Deep Neural Networks
status_evidence.snippet: ReLU networks are equivalent to tropical rational maps, giving a (max,+)-algebraic view of standard networks.
status_evidence.claim: Tropical/(max,+) algebra captures ReLU networks, suggesting a partial bridge to morphological operators.

status_evidence.title: Morphological Perceptrons: Geometry and Training
status_evidence.snippet: Studies morphological/tropical neural networks and their expressiveness.
status_evidence.claim: Algebraic analysis exists for morphological networks separately, but not a unified theory with standard layers.
